questions.explanation: IV therapy and certain emergency medications are within the advanced EMT scope, which sits above the EMT but below the paramedic.
questions.question: On scene, a provider starts an IV line and gives a patient one of the emergency medicines her training and protocols allow, but she does not perform paramedic-level skills. What level of provider is she?

questions.explanation: That added IV and medication role identifies the advanced EMT.
questions.question: A crew member who has moved one step beyond basic EMT training is authorized to place an IV and administer a limited set of emergency drugs. What is this provider level called?

questions.explanation: The advanced EMT sits between EMT and paramedic, with IV and select medication skills.
questions.question: During a call, the provider giving IV fluids and an approved emergency medication is working above the EMT level but below the paramedic level. Which provider level is this?

questions.explanation: Basic life support, AED use, and medication assistance are core EMT functions.
questions.question: A provider gives basic life support, applies an AED to an unresponsive patient, and helps the patient take a prescribed medication. What level of provider is this?

questions.explanation: EMTs provide basic life support, including use of an airway adjunct.
questions.question: At a collapse, a responder inserts an airway adjunct and begins basic life support care while the ambulance is readied for transport. Which provider level does this describe?

questions.explanation: Assisting patients with certain prescribed medications is part of the EMT role.
questions.question: A patient with chest discomfort is assisted with his own prescribed medication by the basic-level field provider caring for him. What is that provider called?

questions.explanation: Procedures beyond basic life support are advanced life support.
questions.question: A patient's care goes beyond basic measures when the crew begins advanced airway and cardiac treatment procedures in the field. What level of care is this called?

questions.explanation: Advanced life-saving procedures define advanced life support care.
questions.question: Instead of only oxygen and basic support, the crew performs advanced life-saving interventions normally associated with higher-level providers. Which type of care are they providing?

questions.explanation: Care that moves past basic life support into advanced procedures is ALS.
questions.question: A critically ill patient receives advanced procedures in the field that some EMTs are now trained to help provide, rather than basic care alone. What is this level of care?

questions.explanation: Selecting units and giving prearrival instructions are emergency medical dispatch functions.
questions.question: When a 911 call comes in, a trained dispatcher decides which units should respond and talks the caller through care until the crew arrives. What system is this?

questions.explanation: Emergency medical dispatch provides caller instructions while crews are en route.
questions.question: A caller is told step by step what to do for a choking child while the dispatcher sends the closest appropriate ambulance. Which dispatch function is being used?

questions.explanation: That unit-selection plus prearrival-instruction role is emergency medical dispatch.
questions.question: Before any crew arrives, dispatch matches the call to the right response units and keeps giving the caller vital instructions by phone. What is this called?

questions.explanation: EMS is the combined team of professionals and agencies providing prehospital care and transport.
questions.question: Dispatchers, first responders, EMTs, paramedics, and hospital staff all work together so a sick patient gets field care and transport to the hospital. What overall system is this?

questions.explanation: That coordinated care-and-transport network is the emergency medical services system.
questions.question: After a car crash, several types of health care professionals and agencies coordinate to treat the injured and move them to definitive care. Which system are they part of?

questions.explanation: Providing emergency care and transportation to the sick and injured is the EMS mission.
questions.question: A community relies on an organized team of health care professionals to answer medical emergencies, care for the sick and injured, and transport them. What is that team called?

choices: They kept the EMT-I/85 level indefinitely
They lost all EMS certification permanently
questions.explanation: I/85s who missed their transition deadlines (2015-2017) were recertified as EMTs.
questions.question: In 2011 the NREMT adopted a transition policy after the National EMS Scope of Practice Model created the Advanced EMT level to replace the many EMT-Intermediate levels. What happened to EMT-I/85 providers who missed their transition deadline?

choices: Intubation doubled survival compared with BVM alone
BVM alone doubled survival compared with intubation
Survival was similar (30% BVM vs. 26% intubation), with no significant difference
questions.explanation: The JAMA 2000 trial found no significant survival difference, showing core EMT ventilation skills are what count.
questions.question: In a Los Angeles and Orange County trial (1994-1997), 830 children who needed airway help received bag-valve-mask (BVM) ventilation only on odd days, or BVM followed by field intubation on even days. What did the study find about survival to hospital discharge?

choices: It did not change (5.0% before ALS vs. 5.1% after)
It doubled once ALS was added
It fell sharply because of intubation delays
It rose mainly because of IV drug administration
questions.explanation: OPALS (NEJM, 2004) found survival unchanged; it was tied instead to witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, and rapid defibrillation.
questions.question: In the OPALS study in Ontario, paramedic ALS (intubation and IV drugs) was added in 17 cities that already had rapid defibrillation. What happened to survival to hospital discharge for cardiac arrest patients?

choices: Bystander CPR fell because callers waited for instructions
Hospital records showed a clear excess of injuries from dispatcher-assisted CPR
Bystander CPR was unchanged by the phone instructions
Bystander CPR rose from 45% to 56%, with no excess injury found
questions.explanation: Dispatcher-assisted CPR raised bystander CPR rates and saved lives, with no excess injury in hospital records.
questions.question: In a 1985 King County, Washington study, dispatchers began giving CPR instructions by phone to callers. What was the effect on bystander CPR?
